This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of N.S. Padmavathi @ Naguru Siddareddy Padmavathi, who is wife of petitioner No.1 and mother of petitioners No.2 to 4, in a road Bhaskar Reddy B R vs Sudhakar Babu G on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18642101/

The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 13-09-2024, at about 3.10 p.m., the deceased N.S. Padmavathi @ Naguru Siddareddy Padmavathi was traveling in the APSRTC bus bearing Reg.
No.AP-03-Z-5419, from Chittoor to Bengaluru along with other passengers, driven by its driver by following all the traffic rules and regulations.

When the said bus was near Mogili Ghat, Bangarupalem Mandalam, on Chittoor-Palamaner NH-69 road,
Chittoor District, Andhrapradesh, at that time one Tata Goods carriage container lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-15-TB-7777, came from the opposite direction i.e.
Palamaner towards Chittoor side, the same being driven by its driver with high speed,
in a rash and negligent manner and due to excess speed lost control over his vehicle and dashed against the said bus. Due to said impact
, the bus got dashed to another lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-03-TE-7619, which was behind the bus.
As a result of which, the deceased along with other six passengers died and some passengers have sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Government Hospital, Chittoor and then she was shifted to Christian Medical College, Ranipet, Vellore, wherein she has died on 15-09-2024, while undergoing treatment.
Earlier to the accident the deceased was running Nandini Boutique Company at Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.70,000/- per month.
She was contributing her entire earnings to her family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Bangarupalem Urban Police have registered the case against the driver of the said container lorry for the offences punishable under Section 106(1), 125(a) and 281 of BNS.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Hence,
they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per anum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has contended that, three vehicles are involved in the alleged accident, but the petitioner has not made the owners and insurers of APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 and lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-7619 as parties to the present petition.
The respective owners and insurers of the said vehicles are necessary parties to the claim petition and the petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Further it is contended that, the petition is filed beyond the limitation period and no proper, cogent reasons have been assigned to condone the delay in filing the claim petition.
Hence, the claim petition is liable to be dismissed.

Further it is contended that,
the alleged accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving on the part of the drivers of all the three vehicles.

If the drivers of all the three vehicles were careful and vigilant, they could have Bhaskar Reddy B R vs Sudhakar Babu G on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18642101/
3 avoided the accident.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777 and dashing the same to the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03- Z-5419, proceeding on the other lane in the opposite direction.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

19. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

20. According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.

sentences.text: The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency, the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
22. Age and income of the deceased:
The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 52 years.

To substantiate the same, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card of deceased N.S. Padmavathi @ Naguru Siddareddy Padmavathi, which is marked as Ex.P.11,
wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 19-06-1972.
The accident has taken place on 13-09-2024.
This clearly goes to show that, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased was about 52 years.

The petitioners have stated that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and she was running Nandini Boutique Company at Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.70,000/- per month.

To substantiate the same, they have produced registration certificate of establishment, UDYAM registration certificate, income tax return acknowledgments for the year 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024- 25 and bank account statement of deceased, which are marked as Ex.P.12 to 14 and 22.
The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the deceased was running Nandini Boutique and was earning a sum of Rs.5,35,830/- per annum.

There is absolutely no rebuttal or contrary evidence on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners, with respect to avocation and income of the deceased.

Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners and hold that,
as on the date of death the income of the deceased was Rs.5,35,830/- per annum.
23.

Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the legal heirs of deceased are also entitled for future prospects of the deceased, though she was not a permanent employee as on the date of death.

Compensation under conventional heads:
In the present case, admittedly the petitioner No.1 is husband and petitioners No.2 to 4 are children of deceased N.S. Padmavathi @ Naguru Siddareddy Padmavathi.
